cases.sentence: В ___, надо отдохнуть, а то этак ног не хватит.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The doctor walked about, looked at things, ate and drank, but he had all the while one feeling: annoyance with Mihail Averyanitch. He longed to have a rest from his friend, to get away from him, to hide himself, while the friend thought it was his duty not to let the doctor move a step away from him, and to provide him with as many distractions as possible. When there was nothing to look at he entertained him with conversation. For two days Andrey Yefimitch endured it, but on the third he announced to his friend that he was ill and wanted to stay at home for the whole day; his friend replied that in that case he would stay too—that really he needed rest, for he was run off his legs already. Andrey Yefimitch lay on the sofa, with his face to the back, and clenching his teeth, listened to his friend, who assured him with heat that sooner or later France would certainly thrash Germany, that there were a great many scoundrels in Moscow, and that it was impossible to judge of a horse’s quality by its outward appearance. The doctor began to have a buzzing in his ears and palpitations of the heart, but out of delicacy could not bring himself to beg his friend to go away or hold his tongue. Fortunately Mihail Averyanitch grew weary of sitting in the hotel room, and after dinner he went out for a walk.

cases.sentence: ___ изменил богу, вероятно, потому, что захотел одиночества, которого не знают ангелы.
cases.explain: «Падший ангел» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: As soon as he was alone Andrey Yefimitch abandoned himself to a feeling of relief. How pleasant to lie motionless on the sofa and to know that one is alone in the room! Real happiness is impossible without solitude. The fallen angel betrayed God probably because he longed for solitude, of which the angels know nothing. Andrey Yefimitch wanted to think about what he had seen and heard during the last few days, but he could not get Mihail Averyanitch out of his head.

cases.sentence: «А ведь он взял отпуск и поехал со мной из дружбы, из великодушия, – думал доктор с досадой. – Хуже нет ничего, как эта ___.
cases.explain: «дружеская опека» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, he has taken a holiday and come with me out of friendship, out of generosity,” thought the doctor with vexation; “nothing could be worse than this friendly supervision. I suppose he is good-natured and generous and a lively fellow, but he is a bore. An insufferable bore. In the same way there are people who never say anything but what is clever and good, yet one feels that they are dull-witted people.”

cases.sentence: Так же вот бывают люди, которые всегда говорят одни только умные и хорошие слова, но чувствуешь, что они ___».
cases.explain: «тупые люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, he has taken a holiday and come with me out of friendship, out of generosity,” thought the doctor with vexation; “nothing could be worse than this friendly supervision. I suppose he is good-natured and generous and a lively fellow, but he is a bore. An insufferable bore. In the same way there are people who never say anything but what is clever and good, yet one feels that they are dull-witted people.”

cases.sentence: И в Петербурге то же самое: он по ___ не выходил из номера, лежал на диване и вставал только затем, чтобы выпить пива.
cases.explain: «целым дням» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was the same thing in Petersburg too; for whole days together he did not leave the hotel room, but lay on the sofa and only got up to drink beer.

cases.sentence: – Дорогой мой, зачем я туда поеду? – говорил Андрей Ефимыч ___. – Поезжайте одни, а мне позвольте ехать домой!
cases.explain: «умоляющим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “My dear man, what should I go there for?” said Andrey Yefimitch in an imploring voice. “You go alone and let me get home! I entreat you!”

cases.sentence: – Ни под каким видом! – протестовал Михаил Аверьяныч. – Это ___.
cases.explain: «изумительный город» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “On no account,” protested Mihail Averyanitch. “It’s a marvellous town.”

cases.sentence: Походив еще немного, он схватил себя за голову и произнес ___:
cases.explain: «трагическим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: After walking up and down a little longer he clutched his head in both hands and pronounced in a tragic voice: “Yes, honour before everything! Accursed be the moment when the idea first entered my head to visit this Babylon! My dear friend,” he added, addressing the doctor, “you may despise me, I have played and lost; lend me five hundred roubles!”

cases.sentence: Ни одной минуты я не желаю остаться в этом ___.
cases.explain: «проклятом городе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “My honour is saved. Let us go, my friend; I do not care to remain another hour in this accursed town. Scoundrels! Austrian spies!”

cases.sentence: Когда приятели вернулись в свой город, был уже ноябрь и на улицах лежал ___.
cases.explain: «глубокий снег» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: By the time the friends were back in their own town it was November, and deep snow was lying in the streets. Dr. Hobotov had Andrey Yefimitch’s post; he was still living in his old lodgings, waiting for Andrey Yefimitch to arrive and clear out of the hospital apartments. The plain woman whom he called his cook was already established in one of the lodges.

cases.sentence: ___, которую он называл своею кухаркой, уже жила в одном из флигелей.
cases.explain: «Некрасивая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: By the time the friends were back in their own town it was November, and deep snow was lying in the streets. Dr. Hobotov had Andrey Yefimitch’s post; he was still living in his old lodgings, waiting for Andrey Yefimitch to arrive and clear out of the hospital apartments. The plain woman whom he called his cook was already established in one of the lodges.

cases.sentence: Говорили, что ___ поссорилась со смотрителем и этот будто бы ползал перед нею на коленях, прося прощения.
cases.explain: «некрасивая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Fresh scandals about the hospital were going the round of the town. It was said that the plain woman had quarrelled with the superintendent, and that the latter had crawled on his knees before her begging forgiveness. On the very first day he arrived Andrey Yefimitch had to look out for lodgings.
